fields.userName: Fill out the total character level

𝑺𝒑𝒆𝒄𝒊𝒆𝒔
Type in the name of the species (or select it from the drop-down menu) and its traits and features will be filled out automatically, provided that its a recognized species. You are not limited by the names in the list. Just typing "Drow" will also be recognized, for example.

𝑨𝒍𝒕𝒆𝒓𝒏𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒗𝒆 𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒍𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈
Different, setting-dependent species names are recognized as well. For example, typing "Moon Elf" will result in all the traits and features of the "High Elf" from the Player's Handbook.

𝑪𝒉𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒄𝒊𝒆𝒔
If you change the species, all the features of the previous species will be removed and the features of the new species will be applied.

𝘼𝙣𝙞𝙢𝙖𝙡 𝙃𝙖𝙣𝙙𝙡𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝘽𝙤𝙣𝙪𝙨 𝙈𝙤𝙙𝙞𝙛𝙞𝙚𝙧
The number you type in here will be added to the calculated Animal Handling value.

𝘿𝙮𝙣𝙖𝙢𝙞𝙘 𝙈𝙤𝙙𝙞𝙛𝙞𝙚𝙧𝙨
You can also have the field use ability score modifiers. To do this, use the abbreviations of ability scores (Str, Dex, Con, Int, Wis, Cha, HoS), math operators (+, -, /, *), and numbers.
   For example: '2+Str' or 'Wis+Int'.
Don't worry if you are only able to write one or two letters of an ability score's abbreviation, the field will auto-complete (e.g. typing 'S+1' will result in 'Str+1').

Note that any bonus from "Jack of All Trades" or "Remarkable Athelete" will be added automatically if the appropriate checkbox is checked.

Select this to use the variant rules "Players Make All Rolls", where the DM doesn't make any rolls for attacks or saving throws, but instead the players make those rolls.
 This will turn every AC and DC on the character sheet into a modifier. The calculations are as follows:

𝙀𝙣𝙚𝙢𝙮 𝘼𝙩𝙩𝙖𝙘𝙠 𝙍𝙤𝙡𝙡𝙨
 AC - 12		vs. 10 + enemy Attack Roll modifier
For example:
 15 [AC]		vs. +3 [Attack Roll]	(12-20 hit),
will now become:
 +3 [Defense Roll]	vs. 13 [Attack DC]  	(1-9 hit).

𝙀𝙣𝙚𝙢𝙮 𝙎𝙖𝙫𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙏𝙝𝙧𝙤𝙬𝙨
 Save DC - 8	vs. 14 + enemy Save bonus
 (same bonus as a Spell Attack Roll for simplicity)
For example:
 16 [Save DC]	vs. +2 [Dex Save]  	(14-20 save),
will now become:
 +8 [Check Roll]	vs. 16 [Resist DC]   	(1-7 save).

𝙉𝙤𝙩 𝙐𝙨𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙈𝙖𝙩𝙝 𝙁𝙧𝙤𝙢 𝙐𝙣𝙚𝙖𝙧𝙩𝙝𝙚𝙙 𝘼𝙧𝙘𝙖𝙣𝙖
 The math used in the Unearthed Arcana article 'Variant Rules' from 2015/06/08 is incorrect. It changes the chances of an attack or spell working. Thus, different formulas are used here, so that the inherent chance doesn't change. If you want to check the math yourself, take a look at https://rpg.stackexchange.com/a/145293/59760

fields.userName: Write the number of experience points that your character had at the moment of its creation.

Write the number of experience points that have been gained.

You can fill the field out as a formula such as "75+10*50".
You can use both dots and commas as a decimal separator, but you can't use any thousand separators.

Write the amount of gold that your character had at the moment of its creation.

Note that you need to write this number in gold pieces.
You can use decimals, using either dots or commas, but you can't use any thousand separators.

Write the amount of gold that has been gained, lost, or spent.

You can fill the field out as a formula such as "4*50-150".

Note that you need to write this number in gold pieces.
You can use both dots and commas as a decimal separator, but you can't use any thousand separators.

Write the number of downtime days that your character had at the moment of its creation.

Note that you need to write this number in days.

Write the number of downtime days that have been gained or spent.

You can fill the field out as a formula such as "10/2-5".

Note that you need to write this number in days.
You can use both dots and commas as a decimal separator, but you can't use any thousand separators.
Write the number of renown points that your character had at the moment of its creation.

Write the number of renown points that have been gained or lost.

You can fill the field out as a formula such as "+4-1*2".
You can use both dots and commas as a decimal separator, but you can't use any thousand separators.
Write the number of magic items that your character had at the moment of its creation, including consumable magic items.

Write the number of magic items that have been gained, lost, or used, including consumable magic items.
Make sure that you write the names of the magic items you lost/gained/used in the notes as well.

You can fill the field out as a formula such as "-2+4".
You can use both dots and commas as a decimal separator, but you can't use any thousand separators.

Write the date of the session or event here, using the format "Year-Month-Day".

How the field is displayed is controled with the "Logsheet Options" button above, but the format you have to enter it in is always the same.

Write the name of the adventure you played or DM'd.

Alternatively, you can write what happened to your character, such as "Story Origin", "Character Rebuild", or "Downtime Catchup".

Write the number of the session in the adventure.

If you are doing a one-time adventure that is separate from the continued campaign you are in, write "1 of 1".

For non-sessions such as rebuilding a character or downtime activity, write "Special", "Session 0", or leave it blank.

Write the name and the DCI number of the Dungeon Master for this adventure.

For a story origin, you can put the full name of your story origin, i.e. "Rage of Demon".

Here you can put notes pertaining to key scenes, key goals, or important points you want to remember.

You can select the naming of this header. Alternatively, you can type in whatever you want, you are not restricted by the entries.

Note that changing this field has no effect on the companion.
If you want to have the creature on this page use the special rules of Find Familiar, Ranger's Companion, Find Steed, Pact of the Chain, or something similar, use the "Companion Options" button at the top of the page.

Type (or select) the name of the race you want to have on this page. Note that first a list of player species is given, followed by an alphabetical list of creatures. You are not limited by the names in the list. Just typing "Drow" will also be recognized, for example.

𝑺𝒆𝒍𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂 𝒄𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆
All information of the creature will automatically be added. This includes ability scores, proficiencies, senses, weapons, etc. You can change the things afterwards.
Because not all creatures need the same amount of space for all their feature text,some fields may overflow. You can manually edit these fields so that everything is visible when printed (e.g. move things to the "Noted" below).

𝑺𝒆𝒍𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂 𝒑𝒍𝒂𝒚𝒆𝒓 𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒄𝒊𝒆𝒔
All the same things as selecting a player species on the first page will happen, with the exception that no limited feature or ability DC is added as there is no room for that.

𝑪𝒉𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒆
If you entered a race that was recognized and then change the entry to something that is not recognized, all the features and abilities of the recognized race will remain in place. This way, you can change the name of the race to something, while keeping the stats of something else. For example, you can choose "Frog" and then change it to "Salamander", creating a salamander with the stats of a frog.

Type in the name of the attack (or select it from the drop-down menu) and all its attributes will be filled out automatically, provided that its a recognized attack.
